verses.1:1: The words of Amos, who was among the sheep breeders from Tekoa, which he saw in vision concerning Israel during the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and during the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.1:2: And he said, "From Zion the LORD roars, and from Jerusalem He gives forth His voice; and the shepherds' pastures mourn, and the peak of Carmel dries up."
verses.1:3: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Damascus, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with sharp iron sledges.
verses.1:4: So I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the citadels of Ben-hadad.
verses.1:5: And I will break the crossbar of Damascus, and I will cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven and the one holding the scepter from Beth-eden; and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir," says the LORD.
verses.1:6: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Gaza, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they carried an entire captive community into exile to hand them over to Edom.
verses.1:7: So I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its citadels.
verses.1:8: And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the one holding the scepter from Ashkelon; and I will turn My hand back against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish," says the Lord GOD.
verses.1:9: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Tyre, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they handed over an entire captive community to Edom and did not remember a covenant of brothers.
verses.1:10: So I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its citadels."
verses.1:11: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Edom, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and ruined his compassion, and his anger tore continually, and he kept his fury endlessly.
verses.1:12: So I will send fire upon Teman, and it will devour the citadels of Bozrah."
verses.1:13: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of the sons of Ammon, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to widen their border.
verses.1:14: So I will kindle fire on the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its citadels, with a war cry on a day of battle, with a gale on a day of whirlwind.
verses.1:15: And their king will go into exile, he and his officials together," says the LORD.
verses.2:1: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Moab, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
verses.2:2: So I will send fire upon Moab, and it will devour the citadels of Kerioth; and Moab will die amid uproar, with a war cry, with the sound of a ram's horn.
verses.2:3: And I will cut off the judge from its midst, and I will kill all its officials with him," says the LORD.
verses.2:4: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Judah, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep His statutes, and their lies, after which their fathers walked, caused them to stray.
verses.2:5: So I will send fire upon Judah, and it will devour the citadels of Jerusalem."
verses.2:6: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Israel, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they sell a righteous person for silver and a needy one for a pair of sandals,
verses.2:7: those who trample the head of the weak into the dust of the earth and turn aside the way of the afflicted; and a man and his father go to the young woman, so as to profane My holy name.
verses.2:8: And on garments taken in pledge they stretch themselves out beside every altar, and the wine of those who were fined they drink in the house of their God.
verses.2:9: Yet I destroyed the Amorite from before them, whose height was like the height of cedars, and he was sturdy as the oaks; and I destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from below.
verses.2:10: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and I led you in the wilderness forty years to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
verses.2:11: And I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is it not indeed so, sons of Israel?" declares the LORD.
verses.2:12: "Yet you gave the Nazirites wine to drink, and you commanded the prophets, saying, 'You must not prophesy.'
verses.2:13: Look, I am pressing down beneath you, just as a cart presses down that is full of cut grain.
verses.2:14: And flight will perish from the swift, and the strong will not maintain his strength, and the warrior will not rescue his life.
verses.2:15: And the one wielding the bow will not stand, and the one swift on his feet will not escape, and the one riding the horse will not rescue his life.
verses.2:16: And the strongest of heart among the warriors will flee naked on that day," declares the LORD.
verses.3:1: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
verses.3:2: "You alone have I known out of all the families of the earth; for this reason I will bring punishment upon you for all your iniquities."
verses.3:3: Do two walk together unless they have met by appointment?
verses.3:4: Does a lion roar in the forest if it has no prey? Does a young lion give forth its voice from its lair unless it has captured something?
verses.3:5: Does a bird fall into a snare on the earth when there is no bait for it? Does a snare spring up from the ground without capturing anything at all?
verses.3:6: If a ram's horn is blown in a city, will the people not tremble? If disaster occurs in a city, has the LORD not done it?
verses.3:7: Indeed, the Lord GOD does not do a thing unless He has disclosed His confidential counsel to His servants the prophets.
verses.3:8: A lion has roared; who will not be afraid? The Lord GOD has spoken; who will not prophesy?
verses.3:9: Proclaim to the citadels in Ashdod and to the citadels in the land of Egypt, and say, "Gather on the mountains of Samaria, and see the many tumults in its midst and the oppressions within it."
verses.3:10: "And they do not know how to do what is upright," declares the LORD, "those who hoard violence and plunder in their citadels."
verses.3:11: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says, "An adversary, all around the land! And he will bring down your strength from you, and your citadels will be plundered."
verses.3:12: This is what the LORD says, "Just as the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the sons of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be rescued, with the corner of a bed and the damask of a couch."
verses.3:13: "Hear and bear witness against the house of Jacob," declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts.
verses.3:14: "For on the day I bring punishment upon Israel for its transgressions, I will bring punishment upon the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar will be hacked off and fall to the ground.
verses.3:15: And I will strike down the winter house together with the summer house; the ivory houses will perish, and many houses will vanish," declares the LORD.
verses.4:1: Listen to this word, cows of Bashan who are on Mount Samaria—oppressing the poor, crushing the needy, saying to their masters, "Bring, and let us drink!"
verses.4:2: The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: "Look, days are coming upon you, and they will lift you away with hooks, and the remainder of you with fishhooks.
verses.4:3: And you will go out through breaches, each woman straight ahead of her, and you will be flung toward Harmon," declares the LORD.
verses.4:4: "Come to Bethel and transgress; at Gilgal, multiply transgression! And bring your sacrifices each morning, your tithes every three days.
verses.4:5: And offer up in smoke a thank offering of leavened bread, and proclaim freewill offerings—announce them aloud! For you love it this way, sons of Israel," declares the Lord GOD.
verses.4:6: "And I, too, gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities and a shortage of bread in all your places; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
verses.4:7: "And I, too, withheld the rain from you when three months still remained until the harvest; I would send rain on one city, and on another city I would not send rain. One plot would be rained on, while the plot on which it did not rain would dry up.
verses.4:8: And two or three cities would stagger to one city to drink water, and they would not be satisfied; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
verses.4:9: "I struck you with blight and mildew; the cutting locust kept devouring your many gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
verses.4:10: "I sent pestilence among you in the way of Egypt; I killed your young men by the sword, along with the capture of your horses, and I caused the stench of your camps to rise even into your nostrils; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
verses.4:11: "I overthrew some among you, like God's overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a burning stick rescued from a fire; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
verses.4:12: "Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel; since I will do this to you, make yourself ready to meet your God, Israel!"
verses.4:13: For look—He who forms mountains and creates wind, and tells a person what his thought is, who makes dawn into darkness and treads on the heights of the earth—the LORD, God of hosts, is His name!
verses.5:1: Listen to this word that I raise over you—a lamentation, house of Israel:
verses.5:2: "She has fallen—never again will she rise, virgin Israel! She is abandoned on her soil; there is no one to raise her."
verses.5:3: For this is what the Lord GOD says: "The city that marches out with a thousand will be left with a hundred, and the one that marches out with a hundred will be left with ten, for the house of Israel."
verses.5:4: For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: "Seek Me and live!
verses.5:5: But do not seek Bethel, and do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing."
verses.5:6: Seek the LORD and live, or else He will rush like fire against the house of Joseph, and it will devour, with no one to quench it for Bethel.
verses.5:7: You who turn justice into wormwood and throw righteousness down to the ground!
verses.5:8: He who makes the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out across the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
verses.5:9: It is He who sends devastation flashing against the strong, and devastation comes upon the fortress.
verses.5:10: They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and the one who speaks with integrity they detest.
verses.5:11: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take a levy of grain from him, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted delightful vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
verses.5:12: For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are mighty—harassing the righteous, taking a bribe, and thrusting the needy aside in the gate.
verses.5:13: Therefore the discerning one will stay silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
verses.5:14: Seek good and not evil so that you may live, and in this way the LORD, God of hosts, will be with you, just as you have said.
verses.5:15: Hate evil and love good, and set up justice in the gate; perhaps the LORD, God of hosts, will show favor to the remnant of Joseph.
verses.5:16: Therefore this is what the LORD, God of hosts, the Lord, says: "In all public squares there will be wailing, and in all streets they will say, 'Alas! Alas!' And they will call the farmer to mourning, and proclaim wailing to those who know lamentation;
verses.5:17: and in all vineyards there will be wailing, because I will pass through your midst," says the LORD.
verses.5:18: Woe to those who long for the day of the LORD! What use to you is the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light—
verses.5:19: just as when a man flees from a lion, and a bear encounters him, and he enters the house and rests his hand on the wall, and a snake bites him.
verses.5:20: Is the day of the LORD not darkness and not light, and gloom with no radiance in it?
verses.5:21: "I hate, I spurn your festivals, and I will not delight in your solemn assemblies.
verses.5:22: Even if you offer up burnt offerings to Me and your grain offerings, I will not accept them; and at the peace offering of your fattened animals I will not look.
verses.5:23: Remove from Me the clamor of your songs, and I will not listen to the melody of your harps.
verses.5:24: But let justice roll forth like waters, and righteousness like a perennial stream.
verses.5:25: Was it sacrifices and grain offering that you presented to Me in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
verses.5:26: And you will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun, your images, the star of your god that you made for yourselves,
verses.5:27: and I will exile you beyond Damascus," says the LORD—God of hosts is His name.
verses.6:1: Woe to the complacent in Zion and to those who are confident on Mount Samaria, the renowned men of the foremost of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
verses.6:2: Cross over to Calneh and see, and go from there to great Hamath, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms, or is their territory larger than your territory?
verses.6:3: You who thrust away the evil day and bring close the seat of violence!
verses.6:4: Those who lie on ivory beds and sprawl on their couches, eating lambs from a flock and calves from inside a fattening stall,
verses.6:5: who improvise to the tune of the harp, and like David devise instruments of song for themselves,
verses.6:6: who drink from bowls of wine and anoint themselves with the choicest of oils, yet they are not distressed over the shattering of Joseph!
verses.6:7: Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of those who sprawl will cease.
verses.6:8: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself, declares the LORD, God of hosts: "I detest the pride of Jacob, and I hate his citadels; and I will hand over the city and all that fills it."
verses.6:9: And it will happen that if ten men remain in one house, they will die.
verses.6:10: And when his uncle—the one who burns him—lifts him up to bring bones out of the house and says to the one in the deep recesses of the house, "Is anyone still with you?" and he says, "No one," then he will say, "Hush! For one must not invoke the name of the LORD."
verses.6:11: For look, the LORD is commanding, and He will strike the great house into fragments and the small house into fissures.
verses.6:12: Do horses run on a rocky crag, or does anyone plow it with oxen? For you turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood—
verses.6:13: you who rejoice in what is nothing, who say, "Did we not by our own strength take horns for ourselves?"
verses.6:14: "For look, I am raising up against you, house of Israel," declares the LORD, the God of hosts, "a nation—and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah."
verses.7:1: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: look, He was fashioning a swarm of locusts as the late crop was starting to come up, and look, it was the late crop after the king's mowings.
verses.7:2: And it came about, when it finished eating the green plants of the land, that I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand, for he is small?"
verses.7:3: The LORD relented over this. "It will not happen," the LORD said.
verses.7:4: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: look, the Lord GOD was calling to contend by fire, and it consumed the great deep and was consuming the territory.
verses.7:5: Then I said, "Lord GOD, stop, please! How will Jacob stand, for he is small?"
verses.7:6: The LORD relented over this. "This also will not happen," the Lord GOD said.
verses.7:7: This is what He showed me: look, the Lord was standing beside a wall set with a plumb line, and in His hand was a plumb line.
verses.7:8: And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will not pass over them again.
verses.7:9: The high places of Isaac will become desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will lie in ruins, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
verses.7:10: Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land cannot bear all his words.
verses.7:11: For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
verses.7:12: Then Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, flee to the land of Judah; eat bread there, and there prophesy.
verses.7:13: But at Bethel do not prophesy anymore, for it is a king's sanctuary, and it is a house of the kingdom."
verses.7:14: Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, nor am I a son of a prophet; rather, I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
verses.7:15: Yet the LORD took me from behind the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'
verses.7:16: And now, hear the word of the LORD! You are saying, 'You must not prophesy against Israel, and you must not preach against the house of Isaac.'
verses.7:17: Therefore, this is what the LORD says: 'Your wife will act as a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword; your land will be apportioned by a measuring line, and you yourself will die on an unclean land, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
verses.8:1: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: look, a basket of summer fruit.
verses.8:2: And He said, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will not pass over them again.
verses.8:3: And the songs of the temple will wail in that day," declares the Lord GOD. "Many are the corpses! In every place they are cast out. Hush!"
verses.8:4: Hear this, you who trample the needy, to put an end to the poor of the land,
verses.8:5: saying, "When will the new moon pass so that we may sell grain, and the Sabbath so that we may open the wheat, making the ephah small and making the shekel large, and falsifying scales of deceit,
verses.8:6: buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals? And we will sell the sweepings of the wheat!"
verses.8:7: The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob, "I will certainly never forget any of their deeds."
verses.8:8: Will the land not tremble on account of this, and everyone who dwells in it mourn, and all of it rise like the Nile, and be churned up and sink down like the Nile of Egypt?
verses.8:9: "And it will come about in that day," declares the Lord GOD, "that I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth on a day of light.
verses.8:10: And I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into a lament. I will bring sackcloth upon all loins and baldness upon every head, and I will make it like mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day."
verses.8:11: "Look, days are coming," declares the Lord GOD, "when I will send a famine into the land—not a famine for bread and not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.
verses.8:12: And they will stagger from sea to sea, and from north to east; they will roam about to seek the word of the LORD, yet they will not find it.
verses.8:13: In that day the beautiful young women and the young men will grow faint with thirst.
verses.8:14: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, 'As your god lives, Dan,' and, 'As the way of Beersheba lives'—they will fall and will not rise again."
verses.9:1: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said, "Strike the capital so that the thresholds shake, and shatter them upon the heads of all of them; and the last of them I will kill with the sword. Not one fugitive among them will flee, and not one survivor among them will escape.
verses.9:2: If they dig into Sheol, from there My hand will take them; and if they go up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.
verses.9:3: And if they hide on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search and take them; and if they conceal themselves from before My eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
verses.9:4: And if they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them; and I will set My eye upon them for harm and not for good."
verses.9:5: The Lord GOD of hosts is the One who touches the earth and it melts, and all its inhabitants mourn, and the whole of it rises like the Nile and sinks down like the Nile of Egypt,
verses.9:6: the One who builds His upper chambers in the heavens and has founded His vault on the earth, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
verses.9:7: "Are you not like the sons of the Cushites to Me, sons of Israel?" declares the LORD. "Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?"
verses.9:8: "Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground; yet I will not completely destroy the house of Jacob," declares the LORD.
verses.9:9: "For look, I am giving a command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, just as something is shaken in a sieve, and not one pebble will fall to the ground.
verses.9:10: By the sword all the sinners of My people will die, those who say, 'The calamity will not draw near or confront us.'"
verses.9:11: "In that day I will raise up David's fallen booth; I will wall up its breaches, raise up its ruins, and rebuild it as in ancient days,
verses.9:12: so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom My name has been called," declares the LORD, the One who does this.
verses.9:13: "Look, days are coming," declares the LORD, "when the plowman will catch up to the reaper, and the treader of grapes to the one who scatters the seed; and the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will melt.
verses.9:14: And I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel; they will build up desolate cities and dwell in them, and plant vineyards and drink their wine, and make gardens and eat their fruit.
verses.9:15: And I will plant them on their land, and they will not be uprooted again away from their land that I have given to them," says the LORD your God.

notes.1:3: The Hiphil imperfect form of the root for 'turn back' carries an unspecified masculine singular suffix ('it'), referring implicitly to the decreed judgment.
notes.1:5: The Hebrew Qal participle rendered 'inhabitant' (also in 1:8) can also mean 'the one enthroned,' forming a royal parallel with 'the one holding the scepter.'
notes.1:11: The Masoretic Text reads the Qal verb 'tore' (like a beast of prey) rather than 'kept'; the closing Qal perfect of 'keep' ends with a suffix lacking mappiq (or poetic ending), understood as 'he kept it.'
notes.1:15: The Masoretic vocalization reads 'their king'; some ancient versions vocalize the same consonants as 'Milcom,' the Ammonite deity.
notes.2:7: The Qal participle rendered 'trample' (cf. 8:4) can also mean 'pant/gasp after,' yielding 'those who pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the weak.'
notes.2:8: The Hiphil verb 'stretch themselves out' uses the same Hebrew root and stem as 'turn aside' in 2:7, forming an ironic wordplay.
notes.2:13: The Hiphil verb rendered 'pressing down' comes from a rare root occurring only in this verse, meaning either 'press/weigh down' or 'groan/creak under weight'; 'beneath you' may also mean 'in your place.'
notes.3:1: The Masoretic Text shifts abruptly within the sentence from third person ('the LORD has spoken') to first person ('I brought up'), merging the prophet's voice with God's.
notes.3:5: The noun rendered 'bait' denotes the lure or trigger mechanism that springs a snare; the final clause uses an emphatic Qal infinitive absolute with imperfect ('capturing, it does not capture').
notes.3:11: The Masoretic Text uses an abrupt verbless exclamation ('An adversary, and around the land!') rather than a finite verb 'will surround.'
notes.3:12: The Hebrew word rendered 'damask' occurs only here in the Bible and is uncertain in meaning, likely denoting luxury fabric or a cushion/part of a couch; the preposition 'with' may alternatively be read 'on,' modifying 'who dwell.'
notes.3:15: The Hebrew adjective rendered 'many' can also mean 'great' or 'large' in parallel with the winter, summer, and ivory houses.
notes.4:1: The phrase 'their masters' (adōnehem, literally 'their lords/masters,' using a masculine plural suffix for the women) here refers to their husbands, whom each woman addresses with the singular Hiphil imperative 'Bring!'
notes.4:3: The MT vocalizes the verb (we-hishlakhtenah) as an active Hiphil ('you will cast'), though in context it is usually understood passively ('you will be flung') or reflexively ('cast yourselves'). The meaning and location of the rare term 'Harmon' (ha-harmōnah) are uncertain.
notes.4:7: The clause 'on which it did not rain' uses an impersonal third-person feminine singular Hiphil form (tamtir), contrasting with the preceding Niphal passive ('would be rained on,' timmater).
notes.4:9: The word 'many' renders the Hiphil infinitive construct harbōt ('the multiplying/abundance of'), which can also be read adverbially as 'repeatedly.' The noun gazam denotes a cutting or shearing locust.
notes.4:13: The third-person masculine singular suffix on 'his thought' (secho, a rare by-form of siach, 'thought/concern') naturally refers to the human person, though some take it as referring to God's own thought.
notes.5:5: The Hebrew plays on both sanctuary names: Gilgal will surely go into exile (galōh yigleh, Qal infinitive absolute plus imperfect of galah), and Bethel ('House of God') will become 'nothing/trouble' (aven, echoing the derogatory name Beth-aven).
notes.5:9: The rare Hiphil participle ham-mablig (from balag, 'gleam/flash forth') vividly portrays God making sudden devastation flash against the strong.
notes.5:11: The verb 'you trample' renders the hapax Poel infinitive construct bōshaskem, traditionally linked to bus ('trample'), though some compare an Akkadian cognate meaning 'exact a tax.'
notes.5:21: The clause 'I will not delight in' literally reads 'I will not smell' (Hiphil imperfect of ruach/riach), a Hebrew idiom drawn from sacrificial aroma expressing divine acceptance or pleasure.
notes.5:26: The weqatal verb 'you will carry' (u-nesatem) naturally reads as future leading into exile in v. 27, though some take it as past ('you carried'). Sikkuth and Kiyyun reflect Mesopotamian astral deity titles associated with Saturn, vocalized in the MT with the vowels of shiqquts ('detestable idol'), or alternatively nouns meaning 'shrine' and 'pedestal.'
notes.6:5: The verb 'improvise' renders the hapax Qal participle hap-pōretim (from parat), understood as strumming or singing idle, improvised tunes to the harp.
notes.6:7: The noun mirzach ('revelry') denotes an elite drinking feast or banqueting association, attested elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible only in Jeremiah 16:5.
notes.6:10: The Piel participle u-mesarefo ('the one who burns him') is spelled with samekh for sin (from saraf, 'burn'), referring to a relative burning the corpse or funeral spices during the calamity.
notes.6:12: The MT literally asks 'or does one plow with oxen?' (using the rare plural beqarim, 'oxen'), with the rocky crag of the first clause understood as the implied ground being plowed.
notes.6:13: The MT vocalizes 'what is nothing' (le-lō davar) and 'horns' (qarnayim, emblems of military strength) as a double wordplay on two Transjordanian towns recaptured by Israel: Lo-debar and Karnaim.
notes.7:2: The Hebrew idiom mi yaqum ya'aqov (lit. "Who will Jacob stand?") uses mi ("who") adverbially to mean "How will Jacob stand?" (repeated in 7:5).
notes.7:4: The phrase lariv ba'esh uses the root riv ("contend" or "bring a legal dispute"), portraying the Lord GOD summoning judgment by fire; hacheleq ("the territory") literally denotes an allotted portion of land.
notes.7:7: The Hebrew noun anak is traditionally understood as a "plumb line" (a lead or tin weight on a cord for testing a wall), though its Akkadian cognate anaku means "tin," leading some scholars to read a "wall of tin."
notes.7:8: The idiom "I will not pass over them again" (lit. "I will not add again to pass by for him") means the Lord will no longer overlook Israel's offenses or spare them from judgment (repeated in 8:2).
notes.7:14: The verbless Hebrew clauses carry no explicit tense and may be rendered in the present ("I am not a prophet...") or past ("I was not a prophet..."); boles ("tender") is a hapax legomenon denoting one who pinches or punctures sycamore figs to help them ripen.
notes.8:2: The vision turns on a Hebrew wordplay between qayits ("summer fruit," harvested at the end of the season) and qets ("end").
notes.8:3: Hebrew shirot is pointed as "songs" (personified as wailing), though some read "female singers"; the Hiphil verb hishlik ("one casts out") is impersonal and rendered passively, followed by the abrupt interjection has ("Hush!").
notes.8:4: Ketiv reads anve ("the humble/meek of"), while Qere reads aniyye ("the poor/afflicted of"), translated here.
notes.8:8: Ketiv reads venishqah (apparently "and be drenched" or a spelling variant), while Qere reads venishqe'ah ("and sink down," Niphal of shaqa, matching the Qal in 9:5), translated here; ka'or is a shortened spelling of kay'or ("like the Nile," cf. 9:5).
notes.8:14: "The guilt of Samaria" (ashmat Shomron) likely mocks Samaria's idolatrous shrine or plays on the deity name Ashimah (2 Kgs 17:30); "the way of Beersheba" (derekh Be'er-Sheva) refers either to its pilgrimage road or, by comparison with Ugaritic drkt, its patron power.
notes.9:6: Hebrew ma'alotav ("His upper chambers") literally means "His steps/ascents" (heaven's upper chambers, cf. Ps 104:3), and aguddato ("His vault") literally denotes a "band" or "bound structure," depicting the vaulted sky founded on the earth.
notes.9:9: The Niphal verb yinnoa ("is shaken") is impersonal with no explicit subject noun for what is sifted in the sieve (kevarah), and tseror literally denotes a "pebble" (though some interpret it as a "grain/kernel").
notes.9:11: The Hebrew pronominal suffixes shift across the verse—3fp "their breaches," 3ms "his [David's] ruins," and 3fs "rebuild it [the booth]"—smoothed here to "its/it" in English.
notes.9:12: The Masoretic Hebrew reads yirshu ("they may possess") and Edom ("Edom"), continuing the Davidic restoration promise of v. 11.
notes.9:14: The Hebrew idiom shuv shevut ("restore the fortunes") is also frequently connected to the root shavah ("take captive"), meaning "bring back the captivity/exiles."

native_verses.1:1: The words of Amos, who was among the sheep breeders from Tekoa, which he saw in vision concerning Israel during the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and during the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
native_verses.1:2: And he said, "From Zion the LORD roars, and from Jerusalem He gives forth His voice; and the shepherds' pastures mourn, and the peak of Carmel dries up."
native_verses.1:3: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Damascus, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with sharp iron sledges.
native_verses.1:4: So I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the citadels of Ben-hadad.
native_verses.1:5: And I will break the crossbar of Damascus, and I will cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven and the one holding the scepter from Beth-eden; and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir," says the LORD.
native_verses.1:6: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Gaza, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they carried an entire captive community into exile to hand them over to Edom.
native_verses.1:7: So I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its citadels.
native_verses.1:8: And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the one holding the scepter from Ashkelon; and I will turn My hand back against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish," says the Lord GOD.
native_verses.1:9: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Tyre, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they handed over an entire captive community to Edom and did not remember a covenant of brothers.
native_verses.1:10: So I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its citadels."
native_verses.1:11: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Edom, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and ruined his compassion, and his anger tore continually, and he kept his fury endlessly.
native_verses.1:12: So I will send fire upon Teman, and it will devour the citadels of Bozrah."
native_verses.1:13: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of the sons of Ammon, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to widen their border.
native_verses.1:14: So I will kindle fire on the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its citadels, with a war cry on a day of battle, with a gale on a day of whirlwind.
native_verses.1:15: And their king will go into exile, he and his officials together," says the LORD.
native_verses.2:1: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Moab, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
native_verses.2:2: So I will send fire upon Moab, and it will devour the citadels of Kerioth; and Moab will die amid uproar, with a war cry, with the sound of a ram's horn.
native_verses.2:3: And I will cut off the judge from its midst, and I will kill all its officials with him," says the LORD.
native_verses.2:4: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Judah, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep His statutes, and their lies, after which their fathers walked, caused them to stray.
native_verses.2:5: So I will send fire upon Judah, and it will devour the citadels of Jerusalem."
native_verses.2:6: This is what the LORD says, "On account of three transgressions of Israel, and on account of four, I will not turn it back, because they sell a righteous person for silver and a needy one for a pair of sandals,
native_verses.2:7: those who trample the head of the weak into the dust of the earth and turn aside the way of the afflicted; and a man and his father go to the young woman, so as to profane My holy name.
native_verses.2:8: And on garments taken in pledge they stretch themselves out beside every altar, and the wine of those who were fined they drink in the house of their God.
native_verses.2:9: Yet I destroyed the Amorite from before them, whose height was like the height of cedars, and he was sturdy as the oaks; and I destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from below.
native_verses.2:10: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and I led you in the wilderness forty years to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
native_verses.2:11: And I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is it not indeed so, sons of Israel?" declares the LORD.
native_verses.2:12: "Yet you gave the Nazirites wine to drink, and you commanded the prophets, saying, 'You must not prophesy.'
native_verses.2:13: Look, I am pressing down beneath you, just as a cart presses down that is full of cut grain.
native_verses.2:14: And flight will perish from the swift, and the strong will not maintain his strength, and the warrior will not rescue his life.
native_verses.2:15: And the one wielding the bow will not stand, and the one swift on his feet will not escape, and the one riding the horse will not rescue his life.
native_verses.2:16: And the strongest of heart among the warriors will flee naked on that day," declares the LORD.
native_verses.3:1: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
native_verses.3:2: "You alone have I known out of all the families of the earth; for this reason I will bring punishment upon you for all your iniquities."
native_verses.3:3: Do two walk together unless they have met by appointment?
native_verses.3:4: Does a lion roar in the forest if it has no prey? Does a young lion give forth its voice from its lair unless it has captured something?
native_verses.3:5: Does a bird fall into a snare on the earth when there is no bait for it? Does a snare spring up from the ground without capturing anything at all?
native_verses.3:6: If a ram's horn is blown in a city, will the people not tremble? If disaster occurs in a city, has the LORD not done it?
native_verses.3:7: Indeed, the Lord GOD does not do a thing unless He has disclosed His confidential counsel to His servants the prophets.
native_verses.3:8: A lion has roared; who will not be afraid? The Lord GOD has spoken; who will not prophesy?
native_verses.3:9: Proclaim to the citadels in Ashdod and to the citadels in the land of Egypt, and say, "Gather on the mountains of Samaria, and see the many tumults in its midst and the oppressions within it."
native_verses.3:10: "And they do not know how to do what is upright," declares the LORD, "those who hoard violence and plunder in their citadels."
native_verses.3:11: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says, "An adversary, all around the land! And he will bring down your strength from you, and your citadels will be plundered."
native_verses.3:12: This is what the LORD says, "Just as the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the sons of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be rescued, with the corner of a bed and the damask of a couch."
native_verses.3:13: "Hear and bear witness against the house of Jacob," declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts.
native_verses.3:14: "For on the day I bring punishment upon Israel for its transgressions, I will bring punishment upon the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar will be hacked off and fall to the ground.
native_verses.3:15: And I will strike down the winter house together with the summer house; the ivory houses will perish, and many houses will vanish," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:1: Listen to this word, cows of Bashan who are on Mount Samaria—oppressing the poor, crushing the needy, saying to their masters, "Bring, and let us drink!"
native_verses.4:2: The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: "Look, days are coming upon you, and they will lift you away with hooks, and the remainder of you with fishhooks.
native_verses.4:3: And you will go out through breaches, each woman straight ahead of her, and you will be flung toward Harmon," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:4: "Come to Bethel and transgress; at Gilgal, multiply transgression! And bring your sacrifices each morning, your tithes every three days.
native_verses.4:5: And offer up in smoke a thank offering of leavened bread, and proclaim freewill offerings—announce them aloud! For you love it this way, sons of Israel," declares the Lord GOD.
native_verses.4:6: "And I, too, gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities and a shortage of bread in all your places; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:7: "And I, too, withheld the rain from you when three months still remained until the harvest; I would send rain on one city, and on another city I would not send rain. One plot would be rained on, while the plot on which it did not rain would dry up.
native_verses.4:8: And two or three cities would stagger to one city to drink water, and they would not be satisfied; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:9: "I struck you with blight and mildew; the cutting locust kept devouring your many gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:10: "I sent pestilence among you in the way of Egypt; I killed your young men by the sword, along with the capture of your horses, and I caused the stench of your camps to rise even into your nostrils; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:11: "I overthrew some among you, like God's overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a burning stick rescued from a fire; yet you did not turn back to Me," declares the LORD.
native_verses.4:12: "Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel; since I will do this to you, make yourself ready to meet your God, Israel!"
native_verses.4:13: For look—He who forms mountains and creates wind, and tells a person what his thought is, who makes dawn into darkness and treads on the heights of the earth—the LORD, God of hosts, is His name!
native_verses.5:1: Listen to this word that I raise over you—a lamentation, house of Israel:
native_verses.5:2: "She has fallen—never again will she rise, virgin Israel! She is abandoned on her soil; there is no one to raise her."
native_verses.5:3: For this is what the Lord GOD says: "The city that marches out with a thousand will be left with a hundred, and the one that marches out with a hundred will be left with ten, for the house of Israel."
native_verses.5:4: For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: "Seek Me and live!
native_verses.5:5: But do not seek Bethel, and do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing."
native_verses.5:6: Seek the LORD and live, or else He will rush like fire against the house of Joseph, and it will devour, with no one to quench it for Bethel.
native_verses.5:7: You who turn justice into wormwood and throw righteousness down to the ground!
native_verses.5:8: He who makes the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out across the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
native_verses.5:9: It is He who sends devastation flashing against the strong, and devastation comes upon the fortress.
native_verses.5:10: They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and the one who speaks with integrity they detest.
native_verses.5:11: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take a levy of grain from him, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted delightful vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
native_verses.5:12: For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are mighty—harassing the righteous, taking a bribe, and thrusting the needy aside in the gate.
native_verses.5:13: Therefore the discerning one will stay silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
native_verses.5:14: Seek good and not evil so that you may live, and in this way the LORD, God of hosts, will be with you, just as you have said.
native_verses.5:15: Hate evil and love good, and set up justice in the gate; perhaps the LORD, God of hosts, will show favor to the remnant of Joseph.
native_verses.5:16: Therefore this is what the LORD, God of hosts, the Lord, says: "In all public squares there will be wailing, and in all streets they will say, 'Alas! Alas!' And they will call the farmer to mourning, and proclaim wailing to those who know lamentation;
native_verses.5:17: and in all vineyards there will be wailing, because I will pass through your midst," says the LORD.
native_verses.5:18: Woe to those who long for the day of the LORD! What use to you is the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light—
native_verses.5:19: just as when a man flees from a lion, and a bear encounters him, and he enters the house and rests his hand on the wall, and a snake bites him.
native_verses.5:20: Is the day of the LORD not darkness and not light, and gloom with no radiance in it?
native_verses.5:21: "I hate, I spurn your festivals, and I will not delight in your solemn assemblies.
native_verses.5:22: Even if you offer up burnt offerings to Me and your grain offerings, I will not accept them; and at the peace offering of your fattened animals I will not look.
native_verses.5:23: Remove from Me the clamor of your songs, and I will not listen to the melody of your harps.
native_verses.5:24: But let justice roll forth like waters, and righteousness like a perennial stream.
native_verses.5:25: Was it sacrifices and grain offering that you presented to Me in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
native_verses.5:26: And you will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun, your images, the star of your god that you made for yourselves,
native_verses.5:27: and I will exile you beyond Damascus," says the LORD—God of hosts is His name.
native_verses.6:1: Woe to the complacent in Zion and to those who are confident on Mount Samaria, the renowned men of the foremost of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
native_verses.6:2: Cross over to Calneh and see, and go from there to great Hamath, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms, or is their territory larger than your territory?
native_verses.6:3: You who thrust away the evil day and bring close the seat of violence!
native_verses.6:4: Those who lie on ivory beds and sprawl on their couches, eating lambs from a flock and calves from inside a fattening stall,
native_verses.6:5: who improvise to the tune of the harp, and like David devise instruments of song for themselves,
native_verses.6:6: who drink from bowls of wine and anoint themselves with the choicest of oils, yet they are not distressed over the shattering of Joseph!
native_verses.6:7: Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of those who sprawl will cease.
native_verses.6:8: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself, declares the LORD, God of hosts: "I detest the pride of Jacob, and I hate his citadels; and I will hand over the city and all that fills it."
native_verses.6:9: And it will happen that if ten men remain in one house, they will die.
native_verses.6:10: And when his uncle—the one who burns him—lifts him up to bring bones out of the house and says to the one in the deep recesses of the house, "Is anyone still with you?" and he says, "No one," then he will say, "Hush! For one must not invoke the name of the LORD."
native_verses.6:11: For look, the LORD is commanding, and He will strike the great house into fragments and the small house into fissures.
native_verses.6:12: Do horses run on a rocky crag, or does anyone plow it with oxen? For you turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood—
native_verses.6:13: you who rejoice in what is nothing, who say, "Did we not by our own strength take horns for ourselves?"
native_verses.6:14: "For look, I am raising up against you, house of Israel," declares the LORD, the God of hosts, "a nation—and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah."
native_verses.7:1: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: look, He was fashioning a swarm of locusts as the late crop was starting to come up, and look, it was the late crop after the king's mowings.
native_verses.7:2: And it came about, when it finished eating the green plants of the land, that I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand, for he is small?"
native_verses.7:3: The LORD relented over this. "It will not happen," the LORD said.
native_verses.7:4: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: look, the Lord GOD was calling to contend by fire, and it consumed the great deep and was consuming the territory.
native_verses.7:5: Then I said, "Lord GOD, stop, please! How will Jacob stand, for he is small?"
native_verses.7:6: The LORD relented over this. "This also will not happen," the Lord GOD said.
native_verses.7:7: This is what He showed me: look, the Lord was standing beside a wall set with a plumb line, and in His hand was a plumb line.
native_verses.7:8: And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will not pass over them again.
native_verses.7:9: The high places of Isaac will become desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will lie in ruins, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
native_verses.7:10: Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land cannot bear all his words.
native_verses.7:11: For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
native_verses.7:12: Then Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, flee to the land of Judah; eat bread there, and there prophesy.
native_verses.7:13: But at Bethel do not prophesy anymore, for it is a king's sanctuary, and it is a house of the kingdom."
native_verses.7:14: Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, nor am I a son of a prophet; rather, I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
native_verses.7:15: Yet the LORD took me from behind the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'
native_verses.7:16: And now, hear the word of the LORD! You are saying, 'You must not prophesy against Israel, and you must not preach against the house of Isaac.'
native_verses.7:17: Therefore, this is what the LORD says: 'Your wife will act as a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword; your land will be apportioned by a measuring line, and you yourself will die on an unclean land, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
native_verses.8:1: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: look, a basket of summer fruit.
native_verses.8:2: And He said, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will not pass over them again.
native_verses.8:3: And the songs of the temple will wail in that day," declares the Lord GOD. "Many are the corpses! In every place they are cast out. Hush!"
native_verses.8:4: Hear this, you who trample the needy, to put an end to the poor of the land,
native_verses.8:5: saying, "When will the new moon pass so that we may sell grain, and the Sabbath so that we may open the wheat, making the ephah small and making the shekel large, and falsifying scales of deceit,
native_verses.8:6: buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals? And we will sell the sweepings of the wheat!"
native_verses.8:7: The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob, "I will certainly never forget any of their deeds."
native_verses.8:8: Will the land not tremble on account of this, and everyone who dwells in it mourn, and all of it rise like the Nile, and be churned up and sink down like the Nile of Egypt?
native_verses.8:9: "And it will come about in that day," declares the Lord GOD, "that I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth on a day of light.
native_verses.8:10: And I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into a lament. I will bring sackcloth upon all loins and baldness upon every head, and I will make it like mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day."
native_verses.8:11: "Look, days are coming," declares the Lord GOD, "when I will send a famine into the land—not a famine for bread and not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.
native_verses.8:12: And they will stagger from sea to sea, and from north to east; they will roam about to seek the word of the LORD, yet they will not find it.
native_verses.8:13: In that day the beautiful young women and the young men will grow faint with thirst.
native_verses.8:14: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, 'As your god lives, Dan,' and, 'As the way of Beersheba lives'—they will fall and will not rise again."
native_verses.9:1: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said, "Strike the capital so that the thresholds shake, and shatter them upon the heads of all of them; and the last of them I will kill with the sword. Not one fugitive among them will flee, and not one survivor among them will escape.
native_verses.9:2: If they dig into Sheol, from there My hand will take them; and if they go up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.
native_verses.9:3: And if they hide on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search and take them; and if they conceal themselves from before My eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
native_verses.9:4: And if they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them; and I will set My eye upon them for harm and not for good."
native_verses.9:5: The Lord GOD of hosts is the One who touches the earth and it melts, and all its inhabitants mourn, and the whole of it rises like the Nile and sinks down like the Nile of Egypt,
native_verses.9:6: the One who builds His upper chambers in the heavens and has founded His vault on the earth, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
native_verses.9:7: "Are you not like the sons of the Cushites to Me, sons of Israel?" declares the LORD. "Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?"
native_verses.9:8: "Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground; yet I will not completely destroy the house of Jacob," declares the LORD.
native_verses.9:9: "For look, I am giving a command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, just as something is shaken in a sieve, and not one pebble will fall to the ground.
native_verses.9:10: By the sword all the sinners of My people will die, those who say, 'The calamity will not draw near or confront us.'"
native_verses.9:11: "In that day I will raise up David's fallen booth; I will wall up its breaches, raise up its ruins, and rebuild it as in ancient days,
native_verses.9:12: so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom My name has been called," declares the LORD, the One who does this.
native_verses.9:13: "Look, days are coming," declares the LORD, "when the plowman will catch up to the reaper, and the treader of grapes to the one who scatters the seed; and the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will melt.
native_verses.9:14: And I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel; they will build up desolate cities and dwell in them, and plant vineyards and drink their wine, and make gardens and eat their fruit.
native_verses.9:15: And I will plant them on their land, and they will not be uprooted again away from their land that I have given to them," says the LORD your God.

native_notes.1:3: The Hiphil imperfect form of the root for 'turn back' carries an unspecified masculine singular suffix ('it'), referring implicitly to the decreed judgment.
native_notes.1:5: The Hebrew Qal participle rendered 'inhabitant' (also in 1:8) can also mean 'the one enthroned,' forming a royal parallel with 'the one holding the scepter.'
native_notes.1:11: The Masoretic Text reads the Qal verb 'tore' (like a beast of prey) rather than 'kept'; the closing Qal perfect of 'keep' ends with a suffix lacking mappiq (or poetic ending), understood as 'he kept it.'
native_notes.1:15: The Masoretic vocalization reads 'their king'; some ancient versions vocalize the same consonants as 'Milcom,' the Ammonite deity.
native_notes.2:7: The Qal participle rendered 'trample' (cf. 8:4) can also mean 'pant/gasp after,' yielding 'those who pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the weak.'
native_notes.2:8: The Hiphil verb 'stretch themselves out' uses the same Hebrew root and stem as 'turn aside' in 2:7, forming an ironic wordplay.
native_notes.2:13: The Hiphil verb rendered 'pressing down' comes from a rare root occurring only in this verse, meaning either 'press/weigh down' or 'groan/creak under weight'; 'beneath you' may also mean 'in your place.'
native_notes.3:1: The Masoretic Text shifts abruptly within the sentence from third person ('the LORD has spoken') to first person ('I brought up'), merging the prophet's voice with God's.
native_notes.3:5: The noun rendered 'bait' denotes the lure or trigger mechanism that springs a snare; the final clause uses an emphatic Qal infinitive absolute with imperfect ('capturing, it does not capture').
native_notes.3:11: The Masoretic Text uses an abrupt verbless exclamation ('An adversary, and around the land!') rather than a finite verb 'will surround.'
native_notes.3:12: The Hebrew word rendered 'damask' occurs only here in the Bible and is uncertain in meaning, likely denoting luxury fabric or a cushion/part of a couch; the preposition 'with' may alternatively be read 'on,' modifying 'who dwell.'
native_notes.3:15: The Hebrew adjective rendered 'many' can also mean 'great' or 'large' in parallel with the winter, summer, and ivory houses.
native_notes.4:1: The phrase 'their masters' (adōnehem, literally 'their lords/masters,' using a masculine plural suffix for the women) here refers to their husbands, whom each woman addresses with the singular Hiphil imperative 'Bring!'
native_notes.4:3: The MT vocalizes the verb (we-hishlakhtenah) as an active Hiphil ('you will cast'), though in context it is usually understood passively ('you will be flung') or reflexively ('cast yourselves'). The meaning and location of the rare term 'Harmon' (ha-harmōnah) are uncertain.
native_notes.4:7: The clause 'on which it did not rain' uses an impersonal third-person feminine singular Hiphil form (tamtir), contrasting with the preceding Niphal passive ('would be rained on,' timmater).
native_notes.4:9: The word 'many' renders the Hiphil infinitive construct harbōt ('the multiplying/abundance of'), which can also be read adverbially as 'repeatedly.' The noun gazam denotes a cutting or shearing locust.
native_notes.4:13: The third-person masculine singular suffix on 'his thought' (secho, a rare by-form of siach, 'thought/concern') naturally refers to the human person, though some take it as referring to God's own thought.
native_notes.5:5: The Hebrew plays on both sanctuary names: Gilgal will surely go into exile (galōh yigleh, Qal infinitive absolute plus imperfect of galah), and Bethel ('House of God') will become 'nothing/trouble' (aven, echoing the derogatory name Beth-aven).
native_notes.5:9: The rare Hiphil participle ham-mablig (from balag, 'gleam/flash forth') vividly portrays God making sudden devastation flash against the strong.
native_notes.5:11: The verb 'you trample' renders the hapax Poel infinitive construct bōshaskem, traditionally linked to bus ('trample'), though some compare an Akkadian cognate meaning 'exact a tax.'
native_notes.5:21: The clause 'I will not delight in' literally reads 'I will not smell' (Hiphil imperfect of ruach/riach), a Hebrew idiom drawn from sacrificial aroma expressing divine acceptance or pleasure.
native_notes.5:26: The weqatal verb 'you will carry' (u-nesatem) naturally reads as future leading into exile in v. 27, though some take it as past ('you carried'). Sikkuth and Kiyyun reflect Mesopotamian astral deity titles associated with Saturn, vocalized in the MT with the vowels of shiqquts ('detestable idol'), or alternatively nouns meaning 'shrine' and 'pedestal.'
native_notes.6:5: The verb 'improvise' renders the hapax Qal participle hap-pōretim (from parat), understood as strumming or singing idle, improvised tunes to the harp.
native_notes.6:7: The noun mirzach ('revelry') denotes an elite drinking feast or banqueting association, attested elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible only in Jeremiah 16:5.
native_notes.6:10: The Piel participle u-mesarefo ('the one who burns him') is spelled with samekh for sin (from saraf, 'burn'), referring to a relative burning the corpse or funeral spices during the calamity.
native_notes.6:12: The MT literally asks 'or does one plow with oxen?' (using the rare plural beqarim, 'oxen'), with the rocky crag of the first clause understood as the implied ground being plowed.
native_notes.6:13: The MT vocalizes 'what is nothing' (le-lō davar) and 'horns' (qarnayim, emblems of military strength) as a double wordplay on two Transjordanian towns recaptured by Israel: Lo-debar and Karnaim.
native_notes.7:2: The Hebrew idiom mi yaqum ya'aqov (lit. "Who will Jacob stand?") uses mi ("who") adverbially to mean "How will Jacob stand?" (repeated in 7:5).
native_notes.7:4: The phrase lariv ba'esh uses the root riv ("contend" or "bring a legal dispute"), portraying the Lord GOD summoning judgment by fire; hacheleq ("the territory") literally denotes an allotted portion of land.
native_notes.7:7: The Hebrew noun anak is traditionally understood as a "plumb line" (a lead or tin weight on a cord for testing a wall), though its Akkadian cognate anaku means "tin," leading some scholars to read a "wall of tin."
native_notes.7:8: The idiom "I will not pass over them again" (lit. "I will not add again to pass by for him") means the Lord will no longer overlook Israel's offenses or spare them from judgment (repeated in 8:2).
native_notes.7:14: The verbless Hebrew clauses carry no explicit tense and may be rendered in the present ("I am not a prophet...") or past ("I was not a prophet..."); boles ("tender") is a hapax legomenon denoting one who pinches or punctures sycamore figs to help them ripen.
native_notes.8:2: The vision turns on a Hebrew wordplay between qayits ("summer fruit," harvested at the end of the season) and qets ("end").
native_notes.8:3: Hebrew shirot is pointed as "songs" (personified as wailing), though some read "female singers"; the Hiphil verb hishlik ("one casts out") is impersonal and rendered passively, followed by the abrupt interjection has ("Hush!").
native_notes.8:4: Ketiv reads anve ("the humble/meek of"), while Qere reads aniyye ("the poor/afflicted of"), translated here.
native_notes.8:8: Ketiv reads venishqah (apparently "and be drenched" or a spelling variant), while Qere reads venishqe'ah ("and sink down," Niphal of shaqa, matching the Qal in 9:5), translated here; ka'or is a shortened spelling of kay'or ("like the Nile," cf. 9:5).
native_notes.8:14: "The guilt of Samaria" (ashmat Shomron) likely mocks Samaria's idolatrous shrine or plays on the deity name Ashimah (2 Kgs 17:30); "the way of Beersheba" (derekh Be'er-Sheva) refers either to its pilgrimage road or, by comparison with Ugaritic drkt, its patron power.
native_notes.9:6: Hebrew ma'alotav ("His upper chambers") literally means "His steps/ascents" (heaven's upper chambers, cf. Ps 104:3), and aguddato ("His vault") literally denotes a "band" or "bound structure," depicting the vaulted sky founded on the earth.
native_notes.9:9: The Niphal verb yinnoa ("is shaken") is impersonal with no explicit subject noun for what is sifted in the sieve (kevarah), and tseror literally denotes a "pebble" (though some interpret it as a "grain/kernel").
native_notes.9:11: The Hebrew pronominal suffixes shift across the verse—3fp "their breaches," 3ms "his [David's] ruins," and 3fs "rebuild it [the booth]"—smoothed here to "its/it" in English.
native_notes.9:12: The Masoretic Hebrew reads yirshu ("they may possess") and Edom ("Edom"), continuing the Davidic restoration promise of v. 11.
native_notes.9:14: The Hebrew idiom shuv shevut ("restore the fortunes") is also frequently connected to the root shavah ("take captive"), meaning "bring back the captivity/exiles."
